Volksgemeinschaft ( German pronunciation: [ˈfɔlksɡəˌmaɪnʃaft] ⓘ ) is a German expression meaning "people's community", [ 1 ] [ 2 ] "folk community", [ 3 ] "national community", [ 4 ] or "racial community", [ 5 ] depending on the translation of its component term Volk ( cognate with the English word "folk"). This expression originally became popular during World War I as Germans rallied in support of the war, and many experienced "relief that at one fell swoop all social and political divisions could be solved in the great national equation". [ 3 ] The idea of a Volksgemeinschaft was rooted in the notion of uniting people across class divides to achieve a national purpose, [ 6 ] and the hope that national unity would "obliterate all conflicts - between employers and employees, town and countryside, producers and consumers, industry and craft". [ 3 ]
